affected_files.role: primary - line 14: `<script src="https://unpkg.com/lucide@latest"></script>`. `@latest` means each page load fetches whatever version unpkg currently serves — a supply-chain risk (any upstream compromise of the lucide package or unpkg's mirror is immediately live on the marketing page) and a stability risk (breaking changes can ship without warning). Pin to a specific version (e.g. `https://unpkg.com/lucide@0.460.0`) and add a Subresource Integrity (SRI) hash for defense in depth. Verify: `rg -n 'unpkg.com/lucide@latest' landing-page/index.html` exits 1.

analysis.current_implementation: landing-page/index.html:14 — `<script src="https://unpkg.com/lucide@latest"></script>`. The script is used to render the icon glyphs (`<i data-lucide="...">`) via `window.lucide.createIcons()` in the inline script at the bottom of the file. No SRI hash, no version pin.
analysis.limitations: Every page load evaluates whatever JS unpkg currently serves for `lucide@latest`. A compromised lucide release (or a typosquat) would run on the marketing page with full DOM access. The page also has no CSP that would block inline-event handlers from a compromised lucide. Defense in depth: pin a known version AND add an SRI hash.
analysis.change_surface: 1 file, 2-3 line changes. Replace `unpkg.com/lucide@latest` with a pinned version (e.g. `unpkg.com/lucide@0.460.0`) and add `integrity="sha384-..." crossorigin="anonymous"` attributes. The version number must be checked at PR time — `npm view lucide version` gives the latest stable; pick a recent one and freeze. The inline script `if (window.lucide && window.lucide.createIcons) { window.lucide.createIcons(); }` is unchanged.
analysis.root_cause: The landing page was set up with a `@latest` CDN reference as a quick dev shortcut and never pinned. SRI is a known best practice for any externally-hosted JS but is missing.

options.name: Pin version + SRI hash
options.summary: Replace the line with `<script src="https://unpkg.com/lucide@0.460.0" integrity="sha384-..." crossorigin="anonymous"></script>`. Compute the SRI hash with `curl -s https://unpkg.com/lucide@0.460.0 | openssl dgst -sha384 -binary | openssl base64 -A`. Verify: `rg -n 'unpkg.com/lucide@latest' landing-page/index.html` exits 1; manual: load the page in a browser, confirm the icons render and no CSP error appears.
pros: SRI detects tampering (browser refuses to execute a modified script)
cons: SRI hash must be regenerated when bumping the version — a tiny recurring cost
options.risk_details: The accept criterion is structural (no `@latest`); the SRI is a security bonus. If SRI generation is awkward in the dev environment, pinning alone is enough to close the issue.

options.name: Pin version only (skip SRI)
options.summary: Just replace `@latest` with a specific version. No SRI.
cons: No tamper detection — if unpkg's mirror is compromised, the pinned version is still served

options_rejected: Pin version only — SRI is cheap and standard for CDN-loaded scripts
